answer: Verifiable Delay Function gating curbs Sybils by requiring each agent to bind its public key to an epoch beacon and submit a Wesolowski proof of sequential modular squarings before an admission horizon. Because repeated squaring resists parallel speedup, an attacker must tie up a fast execution thread and sustained power per identity within that window. Its main flaw is hardware asymmetry: custom VDF ASICs outpace general CPUs, leaving low-power relays on a windy knoll unable to renew on time.
